That's some good analysis given the information available. The only problem I see with it is the fact that suspended as it was, the trusses should have all been in compression, not tension. That would point to it being a failure of the tensioning rods running through the base structure rather than one of those running through the trusses.

The trusses on the side and the roof formed an arc, helping to support the rest of the bridge. So the trusses next to them would carry tension, not compression, among others.

If you look at the dash cam of the white truck (I think it was also in the video), it looks to me as if tensioning the wrong cable reduced the arc of the roof a little, so that the roof would fail first, right where the tensioning force was applied.

That could be true, but normally that's not how trusses work. Typically the top and bottom structures carry the load and the trusses keep those two load bearing members apart. That's the way airplane wings are designed, and this is loaded very similarly.
There are bridge simulators and similar games where you can easily visualise the forces (some are free). Wings are unsupported on one side, so you don't get the arc.
